prize_parts.citation: For foundational contributions to the theory of nominal rigidities and monetary policy rules, which underpin the modern analysis of monetary policy.

statement.case_for: My preferred part is unchanged: B015 with Woodford, Taylor and Calvo. I have changed how I defend it and how confident I am. The scientific case is that nominal rigidity and rule-based policy explain why monetary policy has real effects and how it should be conducted. Calvo supplied a tractable time-dependent pricing device that made nominal rigidity usable in general equilibrium. Taylor supplied staggered contracts and the policy rule. Woodford integrated these into a microfounded, welfare-based theory of policy. This is the one candidate where the origins of the building blocks and the synthesis can be named as distinct, dated steps, and it has been used and extended over four decades. After the exchange I would narrow the citation to the theory of nominal rigidities and policy rules. It should not claim that the simple New Keynesian model performed well in 2008 or in 2021-23, and it should not claim the estimation and quantification work as part of the discovery. Hjalmarsson and Friberg both argued for that narrower wording, and I now think it is necessary for the part to be coherent. I also treat support from Krusell and Hjalmarsson as no independent evidence of merit. Krusell is a long-standing co-author and IIES colleague. The case has to stand on the record of the contributions.
statement.case_against: The reservations are real and I have not argued them away. Attribution is the largest. Eight names are credited and any trio omits Galí, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets, whose work made the framework estimable and policy-ready. The trio also spans about four decades and three different kinds of contribution: a pricing device, a contract and rule analysis, and a synthesis. Calvo pricing is a modelling device, and the micro evidence on time-dependent versus state-dependent adjustment is mixed. The post-2021 inflation episode and the heterogeneous-agent critique leave the empirical standing of the simple framework open. Four colleagues prefer B038, whose credit set is cleaner and whose microdata testing is more direct. If the committee weights attribution clarity and direct empirical identification above breadth and durability of influence, B038 is a defensible first choice and I would not call it a mistake.

responses.point: Friberg calls Calvo pricing a tractable device and not an empirical finding, notes the mixed micro evidence on time-dependent versus state-dependent adjustment, and says the three contributions are different in kind and separated by decades. He wants the citation settled before a three-name set is accepted.
responses.response: I accept the substance, and my own menu-cost work with you and Ellingsen makes me particularly aware of it. Calvo pricing should be credited as the foundational device that made nominal rigidity tractable in general equilibrium. It should not be credited as a validated description of how firms set prices. On your question of what would confirm or disconfirm the building blocks, I would separate two things. The durable evidence concerns monetary non-neutrality, the persistence of real effects, and the stabilising properties of rule-based policy. The micro evidence on the form of price adjustment bears on the device, and it has not settled the matter. I therefore propose the citation names the theory of nominal rigidities and policy rules and makes no claim about the empirical performance of the simple model. That addresses your point about three kinds of contribution, though I concede it does not remove the decades-long span.

responses.point: Boppart keeps B038 first. He argues that firm heterogeneity is a conceptual break with strong microdata discipline, that it is distinct from the 2008 prize on new trade theory, and that the credit problem is smaller there than in B015. For B015 he says any trio rests on a judgement about what the discovery is.
responses.response: I agree that the choice of trio is a judgement about the discovery and not something the evidence settles. My trio credits the origin of the building blocks and the synthesis. Yours credits the canonical model and its policy analysis, and I said in round 1 that I would not oppose it. I also accept that B038 has the cleaner credit set. On the 2008 overlap and the matching question about earlier macroeconomics prizes on expectations, time consistency and the inflation-unemployment trade-off, I think we should apply one standard to both. As I understand the record, from general knowledge and without independent checking, each is a distinct later step and not a repeat. Neither overlap seems disqualifying to me, but I would not use it to separate B015 from B038. What separates them for me is breadth and durability of influence on practice. What separates them for you is attribution and empirical discipline. That is a real disagreement about weights, not an error by either side.

responses.point: Enflo keeps B038 first. She argues that the qualitative selection and reallocation result is much better supported than any welfare magnitude. She says influence on practice is not the same as a cleanly attributable discovery, and she is open to revising if the B015 attribution can be settled.
responses.response: Your distinction between influence on practice and a cleanly attributable discovery is fair, and it is the main reason I have narrowed my citation. I do not think the B015 attribution can be fully settled. I think it can be bounded by a citation that credits only the origins of nominal rigidity and the policy rule, plus the synthesis, and I have said that omitting the estimation contributors is a cost. Your point that the qualitative selection result is better supported than any magnitude applies to B015 too. The qualitative case for nominal rigidity and rule-based policy is stronger than any particular Phillips-curve slope. That is why I would anchor the B015 citation on the former. I do not claim this fully answers your concern. It lowers the risk of the citation overstating what is established.

responses.point: Strömberg keeps B050 first with Kiyotaki and Moore. He argues the attribution is clean and exact. He also concedes that direct identification of the collateral-amplification channel is mixed, that the 2022 prize overlaps in theme, and that B015 is his main alternative.
responses.response: In round 1 I did not list B050 and said I was open to learning why it deserved a higher place. Your reply and Dreber's moved me, so I now list it as an alternative. The two-name attribution to one 1997 paper is clean, and I agree that Gertler should not be added. I still keep B015 ahead. The collateral channel is theory-led with weaker direct identification, as you say, and its reach into practice is narrower than that of the nominal-rigidity framework. I want to be careful about my own standard. B015 is also partly a framework contribution whose empirical performance is debated, so I should not hold B050 to a stricter test than B015. The difference I am relying on is one of degree: breadth of use in policy, and a longer record of the framework being tested and revised. A committee that puts attribution clarity first could reasonably reverse my order.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson prefers B015 with the same trio. She says the citation should be worded around the theory of nominal rigidities and policy rules and not empirical validation. She also says the cost of omitting estimation contributors such as Christiano-Eichenbaum-Evans and Smets-Wouters is largest on the quantification side.
responses.response: I agree with both points and have adopted the wording. Your remark about where the omission cost falls helps me. It argues for a citation that makes no claim over the estimation phase, so the omitted contributors are not described as lesser. It does not argue for adding names. I also note that your agreement with my trio does not strengthen the case on its own. We reach the same trio from a shared view of what counts as origin plus synthesis, and a colleague who defines the discovery differently, as Boppart and Fredriksson do, reaches a different trio. That is a point about the definition, not about the record.

uncertainties: Whether the committee would accept Woodford, Taylor and Calvo as origin-plus-synthesis, or whether the canonical-model and estimation contributions of Galí, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets are too central for the omission to be defensible.

How much the post-2021 inflation episode and the heterogeneous-agent critique should count against the standing of the framework, as against the standing of the simple representative-agent specification. I treat them as an extension and partial challenge, and I have not resolved this.
Whether a prize spanning about four decades and three kinds of contribution is one coherent discovery.

Whether the committee should weight clean attribution and direct microdata evidence (B038, B050) above breadth and durability of influence on practice. On that weighting my first choice could reasonably be reversed.
Whether the 2008 trade prize, earlier macroeconomics prizes and the 2022 prize reduce the incremental case for B038, B015 and B050 respectively. I would apply one standard to all three.
My assessments rest on general knowledge and the supplied materials. I have not independently verified any claim about the scientific record or the credit history.
statement.conflict_note: I am the committee chair, and I wrote the process summary of round 1, which is not a ruling. I disclose that I am a long-standing co-author and IIES colleague of Per Krusell, who prefers the same trio. I have also co-authored with Timo Boppart on an epidemiological-economic paper and with Richard Friberg on a menu-costs paper. I treat their arguments as evidence only and do not count Krusell's agreement as independent confirmation. I have no listed tie to Woodford, Taylor, Calvo, or the credited names of B038 or B050. In round 1 I listed B021 as an alternative and mentioned proximity to its candidates. My supplied profile does not document that proximity, so it remains an unverified disclosure. I have dropped B021 from my alternatives this round. These ties are disclosed and not adjudicated.
